bounded_statement: Within the supplied files for case:256ce9b8dd475ee95a97, the selected result — an exact two-sided binomial test of 18 natal-tube returns in 24 pooled trips against p0 = 0.5, reported as p = 0.022656 and significant at alpha = 0.05 — treats each of the 24 rows as an independent Bernoulli trial, even though the data description declares bee_tag (8 tagged females) as the independent unit and each female contributes 2 to 4 rows. The pooled trip-level test therefore inflates the effective sample size from 8 independent units to 24 correlated rows, and the reported significance is not supported at the declared unit level: a unit-level reanalysis (6 of 8 females with above-chance natal-return rates; exact two-sided binomial test 6/8 vs 0.5 gives p ≈ 0.289) is not significant.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently presents per-female tallies and the range of trip counts per female (2 to 4), showing the authors surfaced the clustered structure; however, no unit-level test is performed and the selected result relies solely on the pooled trip-level binomial test, so this transparency does not remedy the dependence violation.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: per-female table shown but not used for inference

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to defend the report in three ways. (1) Arithmetic check: recomputing the pooled test from the CSV confirms 18 natal returns in 24 rows and an exact two-sided binomial p ≈ 0.02266 versus p0 = 0.5, so the report accurately describes what the workflow computed — the issue is not a coding or reporting error. (2) Independence defense: I considered whether trips within a female could plausibly be treated as independent trials despite the description naming bee_tag as the independent unit. The observed data contradict this: outcomes cluster strongly within females (B-07 is 0/3, five females are 100%, B-04 is 4/4), which is the pattern expected under within-unit correlation, and the description itself flags repeated rows per female. (3) Robustness defense: I checked whether the significance claim would survive a unit-level analysis. Collapsing each female to whether her natal-return rate exceeds chance gives 6 of 8 females above 0.5; an exact two-sided binomial test of 6/8 versus 0.5 yields p ≈ 0.289, not significant, and with only 8 independent units no binary summary could reach the pooled test's precision. All three defenses fail, so the demonstrated-issue verdict stands.

root_cause: The workflow's build_report function computes hits = sum over all rows and n_trips = len(all rows), then calls binomtest(hits, n_trips, 0.5), pooling every provisioning trip from all 8 females into a single binomial count. The binomial test's validity requires the 24 trials to be independent, but multiple rows share the same bee_tag and the per-female tallies show strong within-female clustering (e.g., B-07 = 0/3, B-04 = 4/4), so repeated entries from the same authorized independent unit (the female bee) were fed into a row-independent procedure without any unit-level aggregation or dependence adjustment.
